data.name: Aedan
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Irish name Aed, meaning 'fire'. In Irish legend, Aedan was the name of several kings and warriors. In Christianity, Aedan is a rare name for boys.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the inner fire of faith and passion.

in_hebrew.name: עדן
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מקור השם עדן בעברית, וזה היה שמו של בנו הבכור של אדם. עדן תואר כמלאך של האל, שהוביל את אדם ואת חוה הפראה לגן העדן. השם עדן כולל רבדין של כבוד ועושר. הוא מסמל חיים, יופי, ואלוהות.

in_greek.name: Αἰδάν
in_greek.meaning: ἡ μαρτυρία, ἡ μαρτυρία τοῦ πνεύματος
in_greek.long_meaning: Ὁ Ὀνομαστίκος Ἀἰδάν προέρχεται ἀπὸ τῆς Ἑβραϊκῆς λέξης עדן, ἡ ὁποία σημαίνει μαρτυρία ἤ μαρτυρία τοῦ πνεύματος. Ἐν τῇ Βραχύτητι, ἡ ἰσχυρὰ μαρτυρία τοῦ ἁγίου ἐστὶ ἡ καρδία τοῦ θεοῦ, ἡ ὁποία κατέστησε τὸν Χριστόν. Ἀἰδάν ἐστι τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τῆς μαρτυρίας, ὅστις ἔχει τὴν τύχη τοῦ μαρτύρου.

in_latin.name: Aedan
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Aedan originem habet e linguā Hebraicā, significans testimonium seu martyrion. In brevitate, fortis testificatio Christi est, quae facta est per cor Dei. Aedan est nomen hominis qui habet fortunam martyrii.

in_english.name: Aedan
in_english.long_meaning: The name Aedan originates from the Hebrew language, meaning testimony or martyrdom. In its essence, the strong testimony of Christ is the heart of God, which made Him a martyr. Aedan is the name of a person who has the fortune of being a martyr, and it symbolizes the idea of bearing witness to the truth.

biblical_reference.note: The name Aedan is not found in the Bible, but it is a name that has been used in Christian tradition.

saint_reference.note: Saint Aedan of Ferns was an Irish bishop and saint who lived in the 6th century. He was known for his piety and his work in spreading Christianity throughout Ireland.

data.cultural_impact: The name Aedan, originating from the Irish word Aed, which means 'fire', historically holds significant cultural impact through its association with remarkable heroes and kings in Irish mythology. Aedan signifies strength, courage, and passion, much like the fiery element itself. The acknowledgement and praise of these warrior figures instilled a sense of pride and valor in their people, shaping their cultural identity.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian beliefs, Aedan is a unique reminder of the divine fire that burns within each individual. This internal fire signifies God's presence and love within us. Drawing inspiration from the biblical phrase, "I have come to bring fire on the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled", (Luke 12:49), the spiritual significance of the name Aedan represents the call to live with fervor and passion for God. Embracing this inner fire strengthens our faith and commitment to the Lord.

historical_references.reference: Aedan mac Gabrán was a King of Dál Riata in Scotland, traditionally regarded as the founder of the Kingdom of Dalriada. He is believed to have reigned from approximately 572 AD to 608 AD. According to legend, Aedan was an illegitimate son of Gabrán, King of Dál Riata, and a Scottish nun. He was educated in Iona, an island off the west coast of Scotland, by St. Columba, who later became a mentor to him. Aedan eventually succeeded his father as King and is known for his victories over the Picts.
historical_references.context: King of Dál Riata in Scotland

historical_references.reference: Aedan mac Gorathe was a King of the Scots, who reigned from approximately 878 AD to 893 AD, according to Irish annals. He was the son of Gorathe, a King of the Scots, and succeeded his father. Aedan is best known for his defeat of Constantine II, King of Alba, in the Battle of Boarhaven in 893 AD, which ended a period of conflict between the two kingdoms. The battle took place in the area of modern-day East Lothian, Scotland.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Aedan is of Irish origin and means 'little fire'. In modern contexts, it is often associated with Irish mythology and historical figures. In books, Aedan is a popular name for characters in historical fiction and fantasy genres. For instance, Aedan Dugan from the novel 'The Last Druid' and Aedan MacRory from 'The Thief's Daughter'. In television shows and movies, Aedan is portrayed as a powerful and noble character, such as King Aethelstan in 'The Last Kingdom' series or Aedan Mullett in 'Outlander'. In video games, Aedan is a common name for brave and heroic characters, like Aedan in 'Kingdoms of Amalur: Reckoning' and 'Dragon Age: Inquisition'.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named James Aedan in London, United Kingdom credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Aedan, which means "little fire". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Aedan, meaning "little fire," represents the inner spiritual flame that ignites passion for God and illumines the path towards righteousness. It is a reminder of the divine spark within each believer, inspiring courage and determination in the face of challenges.
